solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Produced note before the signal to stop

indicators.note: placed ahead of the rest of the letters in the word order

parts.note: fa is a note of the sol-fa scale
a red light is the signal for traffic to halt

explanation.surface: Someone produced a musical note just ahead of being flagged to stop.
explanation.definitionFit: To father a child is to beget or produce one, so the past tense matches 'Produced'.

clue.text: Strange tales about firm that once flavoured beer

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the abbreviation for the firm
strange suggests the letters of tales are in an odd, rearranged order

parts.note: CO is the usual abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: Odd stories surround a company that used to add flavour to brewing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' signals the anagram (giving ALEST) and 'about' the wrap; the definition is a description rather than a synonym, fair because the herb's name records its use in ale.
explanation.definitionFit: Alecost, or costmary, is a herb historically put into ale as a flavouring, hence its name.

clue.text: Physician in box carried by massive animals

indicators.note: the box sits inside the animals, as if they bear it

parts.note: hippos are huge African river mammals
a crate is a wooden box

explanation.surface: A doctor is found in a crate being hauled by enormous beasts.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek father of medicine is the archetypal physician, remembered in the oath doctors take.

clue.text: Former Kent player always up to conserve energy

indicators.note: conserve means keep inside, so the energy symbol is held within
in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An old Kent cricketer is always keen to save his strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns EVER into REVE, and 'to conserve' places E inside it. 'Kent' suggests the county cricket side, but the player is the late actor Christopher Reeve, who played Clark Kent in the Superman films.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Reeve, now dead, portrayed Superman's alter ego Clark Kent on screen.

clue.text: Kid has repaired one African garment

indicators.note: repaired suggests the letters of 'Kid has' have been put back together differently

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A child has mended a single item of African clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A dashiki is a loose, colourful tunic worn in West Africa.

clue.text: Coin in large pot

definitions.meaning: a low-value British penny or twopence, made of bronze, is called this informally
a big metal boiler once used for laundry was named after the metal it was made of

explanation.surface: A coin is dropped into a big pot.
explanation.definitionFit: The metal names both small change and the big boiling vessel of old washhouses.

clue.text: Old European to sing about good in humans

indicators.note: the singing word wraps round the other letters

parts.note: to croon is to sing softly

indicators.note: the good letter goes inside the word for humans

parts.note: man means humankind as a whole

explanation.surface: An ancient European is urged to sing about the good in people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' gives MAGN and 'about' signals the wrap; 'humans' looks like part of the surface's moral, but it is the word for mankind.
explanation.definitionFit: Cro-Magnon people were early modern humans who lived in Ice Age Europe.

clue.text: Homer's initial appears in irrational letter to Greeks

indicators.note: the letter turns up inside the irrational number

parts.note: pi is the best-known irrational number

indicators.note: initial means the first letter of Homer's name

explanation.surface: Homer's opening letter shows up in an illogical message to the Greeks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'irrational' looks like an adjective for 'letter', but it is the number pi.
explanation.definitionFit: Phi is the twenty-first letter of the Greek alphabet, so it is a letter to Greek readers.

clue.text: Plea for short dash to provide medical help

definitions.note: Chambers gives an old noun sense meaning an entreaty

parts.note: an en dash is the shorter typographic dash, called an en
to treat a patient is to give medical care

explanation.surface: An appeal for a quick sprint to bring medical aid.
explanation.walkthrough: The en dash (–) is shorter than the em dash (—).
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic noun sense means a pleading request, the same as an appeal.

clue.text: Painter needing one paper getting another on first

parts.note: the Daily Express is a British newspaper
another one, taken as a second 'one', gives the Roman numeral I
1st written with I for 1

explanation.surface: An artist needs one newspaper and then gets another put on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' is another 'one', so I; 'first' is 1ST with the digit as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Expressionists such as Munch painted distorted forms to convey emotion, so one is a painter.

clue.text: Laughing Stalin set about military leaders

indicators.note: the name is placed around the officers' letters

parts.note: Stalin was nicknamed Uncle Joe
COs are commanding officers

explanation.surface: A chuckling Stalin surrounds himself with his generals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set about' is the containment signal; Stalin's Western wartime nickname was Uncle Joe.
explanation.definitionFit: Jocose means playful and jesting, given to joking and laughter.

clue.text: Fancied slogan for subversive reporter?

definitions.meaning: thought up in the mind, as in 'she fancied she heard a noise'
split into three words, it is a journalist's rebel cry of opposing the editor, using the dialect agin for against

explanation.surface: Someone dreamt up a motto for a rebellious journalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Agin' is dialect for 'against', and Ed is short for editor, the reporter's boss.
explanation.definitionFit: To have fancied something is to have pictured it in the mind, a simple synonym.

clue.text: Persistent nuisance lucky to avoid fine

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous pest

indicators.note: the lucky word drops the fine letter

parts.note: fortunate means lucky
F is the pencil grading abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A dogged pest is lucky to escape paying a penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to avoid' removes F from FORTUNATE, leaving ORTUNATE. 'fine' suggests a penalty, but it is only the letter F.
explanation.definitionFit: An importunate person keeps pressing their demands, so is persistent to the point of annoyance.

clue.text: Desperate need to put a Bible in the post

indicators.note: the A and the Bible letters go inside the word for post

parts.note: a post is a station, as in a duty station or police post
RV is the Revised Version of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone badly needs to mail a Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'post' suggests mail, but it is a place of duty, a station.
explanation.definitionFit: Starvation is extreme hunger, a desperate lack of food.

clue.text: Sweetener when wise man loses head over rotten meat

indicators.note: in a down clue the first part sits above the second
the first letter of the name is dropped

parts.note: Caspar is traditionally one of the three Magi

indicators.note: rotten suggests the letters of meat have gone bad and are jumbled

explanation.surface: A sugar substitute is used when a sage turns his nose up at bad meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses head' takes the C from CASPAR, leaving ASPAR; 'rotten' rearranges MEAT into TAME.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspartame is an artificial sugar substitute used in diet drinks.

clue.text: Horse to follow flawlessly finding way through?

indicators.note: the horse letter comes after the other piece

parts.note: to know something off pat is to know it perfectly
H is slang for heroin, known as horse

explanation.surface: A horse following the leader perfectly finds its route through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse' is the slang for heroin, abbreviated H.
explanation.definitionFit: A path is a track or route, a way to go through somewhere.

clue.text: Better writing from woman husband shunned

indicators.note: the husband's letter is shut out of the name

parts.note: Edith is a woman's name
H is the genealogical abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A woman cut off by her husband produces better prose.
explanation.definitionFit: To revise text is to improve it, the work of an editor.

clue.text: Decrease in expected wind level

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: The wind turned out lower than forecast.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwindle is to grow gradually smaller, so it means to decrease.

clue.text: Weird artist associated with opera in China

indicators.note: the artist and opera go inside the friend

parts.note: china is rhyming slang for mate (china plate), so a pal
RA is a Royal Academician
Norma is an opera by Bellini

explanation.surface: An eccentric painter linked to opera performances in China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country, but in Cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' means mate, so PAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something beyond normal scientific explanation is uncanny or weird.

clue.text: Sally ready to embrace East German

indicators.note: the ready word holds the German word inside it

parts.note: ripe means ready, as fruit ready to eat
Ost is German for east

explanation.surface: Sally is ready to hug a man from East Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sally' looks like a woman's name, but it is a witty remark.
explanation.definitionFit: A sally is a quick witty retort, which is exactly a riposte.

clue.text: Eternal fool to accept point by setter?

indicators.note: the fool takes the other letters inside

parts.note: an ass is a fool

indicators.note: next to, the point following the setter

parts.note: hair gel is something that sets hair, hence the question mark
E is the compass point east

explanation.surface: An immortal idiot agrees to the crossword compiler's point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' suggests the compiler, but it is something that sets, GEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ageless never grows old, so it lasts for all time.

clue.text: Dry skin from here one might take off

definitions.note: a noun for a place, matched by the adverb of place

parts.note: to air laundry is to dry it
to strip is to peel off a covering

explanation.surface: A dry skin you might peel away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take off' suggests removing skin, but it is a plane lifting off.
explanation.definitionFit: A runway for light planes is a place where aircraft lift off.

clue.text: Protein excess ends in muscle expansion

parts.note: a glut is an excess supply

indicators.note: the final letters of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: Too much protein makes your muscles grow.
explanation.definitionFit: Gluten is the protein found in wheat that makes dough elastic.

clue.text: Set to reach maturity, needing to shed weight

indicators.note: a letter must be dropped from the phrase

parts.note: to grow up is to become an adult

explanation.surface: Someone is ready to grow up but must lose some weight.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of things is a collection, a synonym.

clue.text: Changing pants idea is so cool

indicators.note: changing tells us the letters of these words are swapped about

explanation.surface: Putting on different trousers is a calm, relaxed idea.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cool in the sense of unemotional and detached is being impartial and calm.

clue.text: Runner at last conquers Karakoram peak

indicators.note: the final letter of the word conquers

parts.note: K1 is the survey label of Masherbrum, a Karakoram mountain, with the digit 1 read as I

explanation.surface: A runner finally conquers a Himalayan summit.
explanation.walkthrough: Karakoram peaks were numbered by surveyors, K2 being the best known; K1 is Masherbrum.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski is the long runner that slides over snow, as a sledge's runners do.

clue.text: Railway out of extremely pleasant place with canals

indicators.note: the railway letters are taken out

parts.note: very nice means extremely pleasant

explanation.surface: A railway takes you away from a very pleasant canal city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian city is famed for its network of waterways instead of streets.

clue.text: Journalists in tea-shop occasionally drink

indicators.note: the press goes inside the chosen letters
every other letter of tea-shop is taken

parts.note: the press is journalists collectively

explanation.surface: Reporters in a café now and then have a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' takes the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of TEASHOP, giving ESO.
explanation.definitionFit: An espresso is a strong coffee, a drink served in tea-shops and cafés.
